Hi Samir / Lydia —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I’ve put together a lightweight "compact" CAIQ traceability package that should get your security team through initial review without us sending the full binder. The goal: show the control mapping, point to representative artifacts, and include a short narrative for any controls where we have compensating controls or a planned remediation window.

Attached: CAIQ_traceability_compact_v1.csv (mapping + owner + evidence link), evidence_readme.md (how to interpret links / sample extraction instructions), runtime-log-excerpt.txt (example ephemeral log for PII redaction proof).

Proposed delivery steps: 
- Today: share the compact package (attached + Drive link).
- Tomorrow: 30-min walkthrough with your security reviewers (slot suggestions below).
- Friday: hand off any additional evidence flagged during the walkthrough; provide a DocuSign access link if you need signed attestation.

Quick ask for you: can your team confirm which controls they want full artifacts for (if any) after the walkthrough? That will help us prioritize the upload queue.

Scheduling windows (PST): Thu 11:00–12:00, Thu 15:00–16:00, Fri 09:00–10:00. Tell me what works and I’ll send the calendar invite.

Thanks —
Monica Patel

Monica —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the compact format. A few clarifying notes from our side before the walkthrough: 

1) Control scope: we'll likely ask for full artifacts for any controls tied to encryption key lifecycle (CIS-2 equivalent) and multi-tenant isolation (tenant segregation).
2) Evidence format: PDFs are preferred for attestations; logs can be a filtered TXT or CSV as you provided.
3) Redaction: the runtime-log-excerpt looked good — can you add a short note in the readme about how you generated the sample and the redaction steps?

For the walkthrough please book Thu 15:00–15:30 PST. Lydia will join for procurement-only items if we discuss licensing or any DocuSign steps.

Thanks,
Samir
